question: Why is a word remembered better when people complete it themselves, as in hot and c_ld, than when they read it whole?
answer: Because producing it takes effort that reading skips. In the original experiments, words people generated from a cue and a first letter were recalled better than the same words simply read, and the effect has held across dozens of later studies. The flashcard that asks beats the page that tells.
move: Make the material ask you something before it tells you anything.
ask: When I study something, how often do I make myself produce the answer instead of just reading it?
source: Slamecka & Graf, Journal of Experimental Psychology, 1978
reference: Slamecka & Graf, The generation effect: Delineation of a phenomenon, Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory, 1978
